hero.title: Project Manager Resume Skills: *90+ skills* for your resume
hero.lede: The project management skills hiring managers and ATS actually scan for in 2026 — methodologies, planning, risk, budget, and the stakeholder communication that keeps projects on track. Organized by category and experience level, with real examples of how to phrase them. Explore the list, or generate a set tailored to you.

quickAnswer.question: What skills should a project manager put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: Lead with the methodologies you run projects in — Agile, Scrum, Waterfall — then the delivery core: planning, scheduling, risk management, and budgeting. Add the stakeholder and communication skills that keep everyone aligned, name the tools you use (Jira, MS Project, Asana), and note any certifications like PMP or CSM. Tailor the exact mix to the industry and seniority you're targeting.

mistakes.title: Listing duties instead of skills.
mistakes.detail: “Ran standups” is a task. The skill is Agile delivery, facilitation, stakeholder alignment.

mistakes.title: No numbers on scope or budget.
mistakes.detail: PMs are judged on delivery. Show budget size, timeline, or team size you managed.

mistakes.title: Only one methodology.
mistakes.detail: Many teams run hybrid. If you've done Agile and Waterfall, list both.

mistakes.title: Burying your certifications.
mistakes.detail: PMP, CSM, and PRINCE2 are keywords recruiters filter on — surface them clearly.

mistakes.title: Generic soft-skill lists.
mistakes.detail: “Organized” is filler. Prove leadership and communication with a delivered outcome.

mistakes.title: Ignoring the tools.
mistakes.detail: Jira, MS Project, and Asana are scanned by name — include the ones you actually use.

skillsToAvoid.heading: Skills you usually don't need to list
skillsToAvoid.description: For modern project manager roles these are assumed or too generic — including them dilutes your stronger skills. Leave them off unless a specific posting explicitly asks.

faq.q: How many skills should a project manager put on a resume?
faq.a: Aim for 12–16 skills spanning methodology, planning, risk, budget, and communication, plus any certifications. Enough to show you cover the full delivery lifecycle, but curated to what you can defend with a project you actually ran.

faq.q: What are the most important project manager skills?
faq.a: Methodologies (Agile, Scrum, Waterfall), project planning and scheduling, risk management, budget management, and stakeholder communication are the core. Tools like Jira and MS Project, plus certifications like PMP or CSM, round out a strong resume.

faq.q: Should I list PMP or other certifications on my resume?
faq.a: Absolutely — PMP, PRINCE2, CSM, and PMI-ACP are keywords recruiters and ATS filter on. Put them near the top, in your summary or a dedicated line, and include ones you're actively pursuing (marked as “in progress”) if the role values them.

faq.q: Do project managers need Agile and Scrum?
faq.a: For most modern roles, yes. Even outside software, teams run Agile or hybrid delivery, so Scrum, Kanban, and sprint planning are common requirements. List Waterfall too if you've delivered with it — many organizations run both depending on the project.

faq.q: What skills should a junior project manager or coordinator include?
faq.a: Focus on delivery fundamentals you can demonstrate: scheduling, status reporting, milestone tracking, a tool like Jira, and meeting facilitation. Back them with a project you supported. At entry level, evidence you kept work organized and on track beats claiming full budget ownership.

faq.q: How is a project manager resume different from a product manager one?
faq.a: A project manager owns how and when — planning, scheduling, risk, and on-time, on-budget delivery. A product manager owns what and why — strategy, discovery, and product outcomes. They share Agile and stakeholder skills, so emphasize the planning-and-delivery side to read clearly as a project manager.

faq.q: How do I tailor project management skills to a job description?
faq.a: Read the posting and note the methodology (Agile vs Waterfall), the tools, the budget or team scale, and any required certification. Mirror those in your own true words and move them toward the top, since ATS ranks you partly on how well your resume echoes the job's language.
